title: Write the OI class

say.never:
Under those comments, write the first method. Type these three lines:

`public static double getForward() {`

`return -driverController.getLeftY();`

`}`

`public` lets any class call it, `static` lets you call it on the class (`OI.getForward()`), and `double` says it hands back a decimal number. The minus sign is there because pushing the stick forward gives a negative number, and we want forward to be positive.
say.bit: Under the comments, write `public static double getForward() {`, then `return -driverController.getLeftY();`, then `}`. The minus makes forward positive.

say.never:
Sticks never rest at exactly zero, so ignore tiny pushes, just like the deadband you wrote by hand in lesson 1. WPILib has one built in. Change the return line to:

`return MathUtil.applyDeadband(-driverController.getLeftY(), 0.1);`

Anything between -0.1 and 0.1 now counts as 0.
say.bit: Wrap it: `return MathUtil.applyDeadband(-driverController.getLeftY(), 0.1);`. Pushes smaller than 0.1 count as 0.

say.never:
Now the turning method, just below `getForward()`. Type these three lines:

`public static double getTurn() {`

`return MathUtil.applyDeadband(driverController.getLeftX(), 0.1);`

`}`

There is no minus sign this time: the left stick pushed to the right is already positive.
